summary: Eva K. Neumaier works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. By 2006, she was Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary, as well as Professor Emeritus and former Chair of East Asian Studies at the University of Alberta.
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin and held a post at the University of Calgary, attested in 1992.

Eva Tichy is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg, later holding the chair of Indo-European studies at Freiburg (1993–2017).

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her M.A., doctorate, and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She served as maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 2003 and became a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.

Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto under teachers including Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco Varela. His main posts include Toronto, York University, and a professorship at the University of British Columbia.
Eviatar Shulman works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, where he became Chairman of the Department of Comparative Religion in 2009.

Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht and Leiden, where he earned his doctorate under teachers including Uhlenbeck, van Wijk, and Caland. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University from 1939 to 1972.
Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his dissertation at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, and Xiaojie Yang.
Fa Yao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He is attested as a Visiting Lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago for 2026.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will and was appointed maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari University, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Naples, holding posts at Sapporo University and later as Distinguished Professor and Shinto Studies Chair at UCSB.

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the "Federigo Enriques" Department of Mathematics (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1994–2005) and the University of Florence (~2005).
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held a post as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua, Michigan, and Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held research positions at Academia Sinica and professorships at the University of Washington (1949–1969) and the University of Hawaiʻi.
Faren is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong, attested in 2013.

Farzand Ali Durrani was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Peshawar, the University of the Punjab, and the University of London. He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from around 1970 to 1993.

Fawad Khan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies who earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University. He served as Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and institutes in China under Taixu and Amdo Geshe, among others. He directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and led the Buddhist Academy of China.

Federico Squarcini is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held a post at Ca' Foscari University of Venice around 2008 and served as Series Editor for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies around 2012.
